## Source ownership

Resolved source material records own their material IDs and explicitly supplied
physical values. Transport preserves supplied scalar or structured shape and
property presence. A native library name is a lookup or template binding; it
does not take precedence over supplied numeric source properties. Original
physical material identity remains distinct from a selected PEC approximation.

The current project-local AEDT realization supports the following normalized
scalar properties. Relative permittivity, relative permeability, and dielectric
loss tangent are dimensionless.

| Source record field | Native material property | Current realization |
|---|---|---|
| `permittivity` | `permittivity` | Scalar relative permittivity |
| `permeability` | `permeability` | Scalar relative permeability |
| `loss_tangent` | `dielectric_loss_tangent` | Scalar dielectric loss tangent |
| `conductivity` | Unavailable | Source value retained; its unit contract is not established |

Source normalization retains supported source declarations, including the
existing `relative_permittivity` to `permittivity` normalization. This does not
introduce additional aliases or a general unit conversion contract. Requested
conductivity currently fails explicitly at realization rather than assuming
units. Tensors, unit expressions, nonlinear or dispersive property shapes are
not supported by this scalar realization and fail explicitly when requested.
Shape-preserving transport does not establish anisotropic solver support.

## Project-local application

Body-first HFSS uses the prepared geometry's resolved material catalog. Q3D uses
the canonical `metadata/geometry_stack.json` attachment already bound and verified
by its geometry-source cohort. Q3D selects only material IDs referenced by
non-PEC bodies and the background Region. No new public material constructor or
spec field supplies a second catalog.

The runtime applies supplied properties to the owned project's material,
including when the native name already exists. Q3D retains each existing
`PdkMaterial.library_name` assignment. It checks the complete selected catalog
before material writes: two source IDs bound to the same case-insensitive native
name cannot explicitly supply different values for the same native property.
A missing optional property is not a conflicting value. The runtime neither
renames the material to resolve a conflict nor changes global library files.

Direct Q3D inputs without `geometry_source` retain their existing identity-only
library material behavior. Historical inputs and their recorded results acquire
no new numeric material or readback requirement.

## Evidence and limits

Material evidence separates requested properties, applied properties, and
independent native material readback. Native readback uses the material manager's
returned definition; cached material wrapper values do not become independent
observations. Unavailable properties and readback errors remain explicit. An
application record does not establish numerical agreement, convergence,
accuracy, or a material trace on a particular field side.

Conductors selected as PEC follow their existing body or boundary realization;
source conductor identity and physical thickness remain separately recorded.
This approximation does not suppress explicit dielectric loss. Bulk material
loss and separately authored interface or offline EPR loss assumptions retain
their own ownership.

Palace's existing scalar dielectric configuration remains a separate backend
lowering boundary. Preserving source values does not add tensor, dispersion,
conductivity-unit, or general material-unit support to that backend.
